title: Opposition LDF walks out of Kerala Assembly over maritime bill

tea.why: The opposition protested against the passage of the Maritime Board (Amendment) Bill, 2026, alleging it threatens fishing communities.
tea.want: To oppose the Maritime Board (Amendment) Bill and prevent the handover of coastal land to corporate interests.
tea.changed: Oct 28: The Keralam Assembly passed the Maritime Board (Amendment) Bill after the LDF staged a walkout and boycott.

summary: In Thiruvananthapuram, the opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) staged a walkout and boycott in the Keralam Assembly during the passage of the Maritime Board (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan claimed the legislation threatens the constitutional right to life and livelihood of over 10 lakh fishermen across 222 villages. Protesters and opposition figures alleged the Bill facilitates corporate control of ports, creates a Maritime Land Bank through land acquisition, and denies traditional fishers access to the sea. Chief Minister V D Satheesan refuted these claims, stating the amendments are necessary to attract investment, accelerate port-led development, and generate employment.
demands: Protect the constitutional right to life and livelihood of coastal people
Prevent the transfer of coastal land to corporate interests
Maintain traditional access to the sea for fishing communities
response: Chief Minister V D Satheesan defended the legislation, stating the amendments are necessary to attract investment, accelerate port-led development, and generate employment, while refuting allegations that state-controlled land would be indiscriminately handed over to corporate entities.

updates.text: The Keralam Assembly passed the Maritime Board (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amid an opposition boycott and walkout by the LDF.
